sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1976. New Hebrides languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-50. Canberra: ANU. (p. 38 vowel-correspondence table; wordlists 78 Avok, 79 Maxbaxo)

sources.note: Only indirect: p. 38 row 78 Avok gives POc *i > i, ə with note 5 'In unstressed syllables.' (verified on page scan); presupposes stress but never says where it falls; wordlists carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir & Eleanor Ridge. 2025. VanBib: A database of references to resources on Vanuatu languages, version 1.3 (17 Nov 2025; 3593 rows, per-glottocode description type coding, notes from Lynch & Crowley 2001 and Te Reo 68). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.17628152.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: rows = ABVD/Vanuatu Voices/ACD wordlists, Charpentier 1982 atlas, Tryon 1976 (note: 'Listed as a dialect of Ahamb (Axamb) by Tryon 1976 but now considered a separate language'), Lynch 2008 'Liquid vocalization' (study of one feature); no grammar, sketch or phonology entry.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Eleanor Ridge & Lana Takau. 2025. Linguistics in Vanuatu 45 years after Independence. Te Reo 68(2) (Special issue: Vanuatu languages in context): 31-78; with supplementary dataset: VanBib: a database of references to resources on Vanuatu languages, v1.3 (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.17628152).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content; it is a documentation-status survey. It states Avok has no grammatical description of any length; VanBib's avok1244 entries are all wordlists (ABVD Shimelman 2016: Avok 162-99, 162-101, Hokai 162-97a, 162-98, Shiaf; ACD Maxbaxo; Vanuatu Voices Hokai/Hokai 2/Small Island; Tryon 1976; Charpentier 1982) plus two comparative articles (Lynch 2008; Rangelov, Walworth & Barbour 2023). Compiled by Rangelov, the linguist who holds the unpublished 2018 Avok fieldnotes, so it is authoritative on the absence of a description.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Mary Walworth & Julie Barbour. 2023. A multifaceted approach to understanding unexpected sound change: the bilabial trills of Vanuatu's Malekula Island. Diachronica 40(3): 384-432. doi:10.1075/dia.21051.ran
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Table A.1 gives the only Avok source as 'Rangelov (2018) Fieldnotes on Avok and Lamap. Unpublished fieldnotes' and the appendix lists Avok under 'Languages without phonological analysis'.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2020. A grammar of the Ahamb language (Vanuatu). PhD thesis, University of Waikato. sec. 1.2.3 pp. 6-7; sec. 2.6.1 p. 78
sources.note: For Ahamb (neighbour): primary stress mostly on the ultimate syllable. On relatives: p. 78 'Ahamb's closest relative for which an analysis of stress patterns exists is Uluveu (Healey 2013: 31-36)' -- i.e. no stress analysis exists for Avok. Nothing on Avok stress itself.

sources.citation: Aznar, Jocelyn. 2019. Narrer une nabol : la production des textes nisvais en fonction de l'âge et de la situation d'énonciation (Malekula, Vanuatu). Thèse de doctorat, EHESS (Marseille). Vol. 1. Annexes, Tableau 17 'Liste des informations relatives aux langues de Malékula présentées dans la carte 3', pp. 320-321.
sources.note: pointer to Charpentier's atlas only; no phonology of Avok anywhere in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent the full text: Avok/Hokai/Okai occur only in this table, a village list and a myth about 'l'île d'Okai').

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2019. The bilabial-to-linguolabial shift in Southern Oceanic: A subgrouping diagnostic? Oceanic Linguistics 58(2): 292-323. University of Hawai'i Press. DOI 10.1353/ol.2019.0010 (Project MUSE copy).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; only the sporadic fronting of POc *u to u-umlaut after bilabial obstruents (na/bute- 'navel', na/vuc 'banana', na/vus-rong 'bow') and its subgroup membership.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva et al. 2019-. Vanuatu Voices (lexibank/vanuatuvoices CLDF; vanuatuvoices.clld.org): wordlists 'Avok: Hokai' (174 items), 'Avok: Hokai 2' (176), 'Avok: Small Island' (178), recorded A. Shimelman, transcribed L. Waegerle
sources.note: Nothing: broad IPA transcriptions, 0 of 528 forms carry a stress mark; audio online but no prose phonology.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2016. Malakula internal subgrouping: phonological evidence. Oceanic Linguistics 55(2): 399-431.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Historical phonology of all Malakula languages incl. Avok (from Charpentier/Tryon data); Lynch's Malakula papers sometimes state stress position when explaining final-vowel loss.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva. 2016. Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database wordlists 'Avok (Avok) 162-99' (ABVD id 1421), 'Avok (Avok) 162-101', 'Avok (Hokai) 162-97a', 'Avok (Hokai) 162-98', 'Avok (Shiaf)'. In Greenhill, Blust & Gray (eds.), ABVD. Personal-communication field lists (MPI survey 2015-16).
sources.note: wordlist-only: 180 broad-IPA forms, none carries a stress mark (0/180 with ˈ or ˌ); the only prose is the transcription note quoted; no statement on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2014. Unexpected final vowel retention in Malakula. Open Linguistics 1: 1-16; Lynch 2019 LLM 37 (Nese); Lynch 2020 (Uripiv phonological history); Schaefer 2023 UCSB PhD; Hoback 2024 VUW PhD; King, Rangelov & Walworth 2025 JoLE; Rangelov 2019 LDD 16; Birchfield & Pearce 2021 LLM 39 (survey of Malakula stress statements)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent: appears only in maps, cognate tables, neighbour lists; Birchfield & Pearce's survey of published Malakula stress statements does not include Avok. No Avok stress statement.

sources.citation: Healey, David S. 2013. A grammar of Maskelynes: the language of Uluveu Island, Vanuatu. PhD thesis, University of the South Pacific.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Stress analysis is for Maskelynes only; Avokh mentioned only for dialect/relationship judgements (Avokh vs Hokai); nothing on Avok stress.

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2009. *Leo Tuai: a comparative lexical study of North and Central Vanuatu languages. Pacific Linguistics 603.
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 C59 2009
sources.note: Avok appears only as a member of group 16 (Axamb, Avok, Maskelynes, Port Sandwich) and in one cognate note; no Avok phonology or stress line.

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: a new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra: ANU. sec. 3.7.7 Avok, pp. 75-76
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Nothing; states the only sources for Avok are Tryon 1976 wordlists (Avok, Maxbaxo) and Charpentier 1982b's longer list; ~500 speakers.

sources.citation: Charpentier, Jean-Michel. 1987. La numération au Sud-Malakula (Vanuatu). In Donald C. Laycock & Werner Winter (eds), A world of language: papers presented to Professor S. A. Wurm on his 65th birthday, 105-118. Pacific Linguistics C-100. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing. Morpheme-by-morpheme analysis of Avokh numerals (1-9, 10 seŋavür, 11-19 with lav 'take', 20, tens, 100, 1000) in Charpentier's phonetic spelling with no accent marks and no transcription note; scanned of all 14 pages a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/ton/intonation/syllabe/stress/prosod/transcription: no hits. First-hand descriptive (morphological) content on Avok beyond a wordlist, silent on stress and tone.
